turns.reply:
Your consumer complaint draft is saved and ready for download. 

You have a very strong case. You paid Rs 90,000 in full on 3 March 2026, the photographer completely failed to show up on 10 May 2026, and you have both the UPI payment receipt and WhatsApp chats to prove it. You can file a consumer complaint under section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s35]]. Under section 39 of the same Act, you are entitled to a full refund of your money along with compensation for the harassment and mental agony caused [[CPA2019:s39]]. You are also well within the two-year limitation period [[CPA2019:s69]].

### What you need to do before filing:
1. **Fill in the placeholders** in the draft (such as your full name, address, phone number, the photographer's name and business address, and the place of verification).
2. **Attach copies of your proof:** Print out your UPI payment receipt and screenshots of your WhatsApp chats with the photographer.
3. **File the complaint:** You can file this complaint online through the e-Jagriti portal (`e-jagriti.gov.in`) or physically at the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Ernakulam.

Please let me know if you need any adjustments or help preparing a final notice before filing!

# BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, ERNAKULAM

**Consumer Complaint No. _______ of 2026**

**BETWEEN**

[COMPLAINANT NAME],
[COMPLAINANT ADDRESS],
[COMPLAINANT PHONE / EMAIL] ... Complainant

**AND**

[PHOTOGRAPHER NAME],
[PHOTOGRAPHER BUSINESS NAME / ADDRESS],
[PHOTOGRAPHER PHONE / EMAIL] ... Opposite Party

---

### CONSUMER COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019 [[CPA2019:s35]]

**1. Jurisdiction:**
The consideration paid for the services is Rs 90,000, which falls within the jurisdiction of the District Commission under Rule 3 of the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021 [[CPJUR2021:r3]] and section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s34]]. The Opposite Party carries on business within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Commission.

**2. Limitation:**
The cause of action arose on 10 May 2026 when the Opposite Party failed to provide the booked service. This complaint is filed within the limitation period specified under section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s69]].

**3. Facts of the Case:**
(a) On 3 March 2026, the Complainant booked the Opposite Party as a wedding photographer for services on 10 May 2026.
(b) The Complainant paid Rs 90,000 in full on 3 March 2026 via UPI.
(c) On 10 May 2026, the Opposite Party failed to show up at the wedding.
(d) The Opposite Party refuses to refund Rs 90,000 despite WhatsApp chats and requests.

**4. Deficiency in Service:**
The failure of the Opposite Party to render the paid services constitutes a deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

**5. Reliefs Claimed:**
The Complainant prays that this Hon'ble Commission directs the Opposite Party under section 39 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s39]] to:
(a) Refund Rs 90,000;
(b) Pay compensation for mental agony and deficiency in service; and
(c) Pay litigation costs.

**VERIFICATION**

I, [COMPLAINANT NAME], verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 5 are true to my personal knowledge and belief.

Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].


________________________
[COMPLAINANT Name]
Complainant
